independent.summary: `begin` folds a duplicate domain into the existing entry but `end` is an unconditional single delete with no refcount, so when a manual scrape and the nightly LeoRefresh overlap on one domain the first finisher clears the shared entry while the other crawl is still running — `/active` goes empty mid-crawl and the merge gate is blind again; the header comment claims the fold prevents exactly this, which it does not.

The test named "GET /scrape/active rejects an unauthenticated request" exercises only the file's own stubbed `requireAuth` (which returns 401 when `x-test-user` is absent); no production auth code runs, so it asserts the stub rather than the claimed behaviour.

triageGrades.reason: No authentication or authorization logic is added or modified — `requireAuth()`/`isSuperAdmin` on `/active` are untouched; the cited line is a stubbed test helper, not an auth change.
Only a non-secret log-level env var is documented in .env.example; no credentials or key handling.
No billing, Stripe, quota, or pricing code is in the diff.
The only deletions are in-memory Map entries; the chunk/page deletion paths in scrape.js are unchanged.
No external calls added — scraper.js, embeddings, and the socket contract are untouched, and the scraper is stubbed in the test.
No deploy, nixpacks, CI, orchestrator-config, or RUNBOOK files are changed; the added env var is optional with a built-in default.

summary: The local model found nothing in a clean, faithful refactor and was essentially right on substance, but it missed the two minor issues (no refcount on overlapping crawls, a test asserting its own auth stub) and mislabelled auth as touched on the strength of a stub line in the test file.
